appealProcess.title: How appeals work
appealProcess.intro: Six steps run from the complaint to the final decision. Two of them are yours, and most carry a deadline.

steps.title: File a complaint
steps.desc: Complaints about a public safety employee are investigated by the Office of Professional Standards, which is a division inside the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety. You can file online, by phone, in person at any station, or by mail.

steps.title: The investigation and the finding
steps.desc: The Office of Professional Standards completes its investigation within 45 days of the complaint being filed. If more time is needed, the inspector assigned to the case contacts you with an estimated completion date. The findings then go to the Chief of Public Safety for a final determination, and you receive written notice of the outcome. You are also sent a follow up evaluation form, notice of your right to appeal, and a stamped envelope addressed back to the city so you can start an appeal.

links.text: About the Office of Professional Standards

steps.title: File an appeal
steps.desc: If you disagree with the finding, you appeal to the City Manager's Office. Your appeal form and the response letter you received must both be received by the City Manager's Office no later than 15 business days after you received that letter, which is roughly three calendar weeks. Incomplete materials are not processed. There is only one appeal form: the city titles it the City Manager's Office Appeal Form, and the Board's own site refers to it as its appeal form.

steps.title: The hearing
steps.desc: After examining the appeal material, the City Manager refers the matter to the Board, and the City Manager's Office schedules a hearing within 30 business days. The hearing is held no later than 60 business days after the appeal is filed. Present at the hearing are you, a representative from the Office of Professional Standards, a representative from the City Manager's Office, and members of the Board. You may appear in person, and you choose on the appeal form whether the hearing is open to the public or closed. The Board reviews the case materials but does not hear from witnesses other than the Chief of Public Safety or the Chief's designee.

steps.title: The Board's recommendation
steps.desc: The Board deliberates privately and sends a written report to the City Manager no later than 15 business days after the hearing. It can recommend that the Chief's finding be upheld or changed to sustained, and it can ask in writing for further investigation. It cannot impose discipline, and it cannot recommend that discipline be imposed or increased.

steps.title: The City Manager decides
steps.desc: The City Manager holds final authority and may sustain or amend the response made by the Chief of Public Safety and the recommendation made by the Board. You will receive notification of the findings from the City Manager no later than 20 business days after the hearing. The City Manager's decision concludes the appeal process.

body.text: What an appeal can and cannot do

The Board is an outside check on an investigation carried out inside the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety. It cannot discipline anyone. The strongest outcome an appeal can produce is a recommendation to the City Manager that the Chief of Public Safety’s finding be changed to sustained. Decisions about discipline are made separately and are not part of this process.

Whether you can appeal depends entirely on which finding the Chief of Public Safety reached. The finding is named in the written notice you received, so check that letter for the exact wording before you file.

body.label: Sustained
body.value: There was sufficient evidence to prove what you reported. This finding cannot be appealed.

body.label: Not sustained
body.value: The investigation could not prove or disprove what you reported. This finding can be appealed.

body.label: Unfounded
body.value: The investigation proved conclusively that the acts described did not occur. This finding can be appealed.

body.label: Exonerated
body.value: The actions described did occur, but were found to be justified or proper. This finding can be appealed.

body.label: Misconduct not based on complaint
body.value: The investigation uncovered improper job performance unrelated to what you reported. This finding can be appealed.

body.label: Exceptionally cleared
body.value: The complainant did not cooperate with the investigation, or did not provide enough information for it to proceed. The Board names four findings it can hear on appeal and this is not among them. Contact the Board directly if you received this finding.

body.text: The Citizens Public Safety Review and Appeal Board (CPSRAB) provides an opportunity for community members to participate in the oversight of the Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety (KDPS). Established by the City Manager's Office, the Board receives citizen input on appeals filed after KDPS complaint investigations and can inquire into any conduct of a public safety officer in the absence of a complaint.

The Board serves three primary purposes: building community trust and credibility in the public safety complaint process; providing an independent review of complaint dispositions that citizens choose to appeal; and advising the City Manager on improvements to policies, procedures, and community outreach related to the complaint process.
For more information about the Board, its work, and annual reports, visit the Board's independent website: kalamazoocpsrab.org.

items: Receive copies of complaints (with personal information redacted) upon request.
Be updated monthly on the progress of all active complaint investigations by the Office of Professional Standards.
Inquire about any complaint investigation, regardless of the Chief's finding, in the absence of a formal appeal.
Review the complaint reporting process and recommend improvements to the Chief and City Manager.
Monitor the overall fairness of the complaint process for both citizens and public safety employees.
Recommend improvements to the City Manager on policies and procedures implicated in the complaint process.
Assist the Department of Public Safety in preparing community outreach materials about the complaint process.
Establish subcommittees to research and address public safety and community relations issues.
Prepare an annual review covering the number and types of complaints, and assess the thoroughness, accountability, and responsiveness of the complaint process.
Issue reports on police/community relations, racial profiling, and other community climate concerns as needed.
Hold meetings with community leaders and neighborhood associations at least annually.
Organize public forums to discuss community climate and develop action agendas with the Public Safety Chief.
Work with KDPS and community organizations to anticipate and prevent problems through data analysis and recommendations.

body.text: The Board consists of up to 12 members appointed by the City Manager: up to 6 from diverse organizations representing diverse populations and up to 6 at-large members. A quorum requires 51% of active members present.

body.label: Appointment
body.value: All members are appointed by the City Manager. The Chair is named annually by the City Manager; the Vice Chair is recommended by the Chair and approved by the City Manager.

body.label: Term Length
body.value: Members serve 3-year terms, limited to 2 consecutive terms. A 1-year hiatus is required before reappointment.

body.label: Residency
body.value: Full-time City of Kalamazoo residents receive first priority. Non-residents with identifiable interests located in the City receive second priority.

body.label: Time Commitment
body.value: Approximately 5-8 hours per calendar quarter, including monthly meetings, two KDPS ride-alongs or hiring events per year, and two community outreach events per year.

body.label: Disqualifiers
body.value: Members may not hold political office, be a current City employee, work for another law enforcement agency, be a retired or former law enforcement officer, or be an immediate family member of any KDPS personnel.

body.label: Orientation
body.value: Members must attend an orientation session within their first 90 days and attend the Kalamazoo Regional Citizens Academy within the first year of service.
